word:greek-nt:G0067.explanation: Agrippa is the name of Herod Agrippa II.

word:greek-nt:G0089.explanation: Adialeiptōs means unceasingly or without ceasing.

word:greek-nt:G0180.explanation: Akatapaustos means unceasing or not ceasing. Here it describes people who cannot cease from sin.

word:greek-nt:G0210.explanation: This word describes something done unwillingly—not by voluntary choice. It can characterize a person who acts without wanting to do so, or an action carried out without willingness. Its basic sense is therefore “not voluntary” or “unwilling.” In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in 1 Corinthians 9:17. The surrounding verse is needed to explain its particular force there; the word itself supplies the idea of unwillingness.

word:greek-nt:G0324.explanation: Anadechomai means to receive or welcome kindly.

word:greek-nt:G0456.explanation: Anoikodomeō means to rebuild or build up what has fallen or been razed to the ground, as in rebuilding David’s fallen tabernacle and its ruins.

word:greek-nt:G0522.explanation: Apairo means to take away or remove.

word:greek-nt:G0579.explanation: Apobletos means rejected or fit to be cast away.

word:greek-nt:G0597.explanation: This word means “to store up” or “to store up treasure.” It describes the action of deliberately gathering and keeping something valuable for future use. As a verb, it focuses on building up a reserve rather than receiving or using something immediately. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in 1 Timothy 6:19, so its precise force there is understood from that passage’s surrounding words and context.

word:greek-nt:G0711.explanation: “Aristobulus” is a personal name, referring to a man rather than describing an object, action, or quality. In the Greek New Testament, this name occurs once, in Romans 16:10. The name itself does not provide further information about the person’s character, role, or circumstances; those details must come from the surrounding passage, which is not included here. Its possessive rendering in one English translation reflects how the name functions in the sentence, not a different meaning.

word:greek-nt:G0728.explanation: Arrabōn means a deposit or pledge given in advance as a guarantee that the full payment will follow.

word:greek-nt:G0830.explanation: This word means “on one’s own initiative” or “self-chosen.” It describes something undertaken by personal choice, willingly and without another person directing the decision. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs twice, both times in 2 Corinthians 8. Its basic emphasis is that the action comes from the person’s own determination rather than being imposed from outside. The surrounding verse context is needed to explain the specific action being described.

word:greek-nt:G0845.explanation: This word refers to an eyewitness—someone who personally saw what happened and can testify about it. It describes direct, firsthand knowledge rather than information received from another person. The word appears once in the Greek New Testament, in Luke 1:2. Its precise role in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its central meaning remains a person who witnessed events personally.

word:greek-nt:G0988.explanation: Blasphemia means abusive or scurrilous language—blasphemy.

word:greek-nt:G1019.explanation: Bradynō means to be slow or to delay.

word:greek-nt:G1042.explanation: Gabbatha is a proper name, retained in English as “Gabbatha.” It identifies a named location rather than describing an action, quality, or relationship. This word appears once in the Greek New Testament, in John 19:13. Because the available meaning is the name itself and no verse text is provided here, its precise significance in that passage depends on the surrounding context. The word’s ordinary lexical function is therefore simply to designate Gabbatha.

word:greek-nt:G1204.explanation: Deuro means come, calling someone to approach or move toward a person or place. It can also mean now, marking the present time.

word:greek-nt:G1341.explanation: Dikaiokrisia means just judgment or righteous judgment.

word:greek-nt:G1378.explanation: Dogma means a decree, edict, or ordinance.

word:greek-nt:G1415.explanation: Dynatos means powerful when describing a person. It can also describe a thing as possible.

word:greek-nt:G1460.explanation: The word means to dwell among or live among.

word:greek-nt:G1626.explanation: This word refers to an abnormal or untimely birth. It is a noun describing a birth that occurs outside the expected time or manner. In the Greek New Testament, it appears only once, in 1 Corinthians 15:8. Without the surrounding verse text, its specific force in that passage cannot be explained here, but its basic meaning remains focused on an unusual birth or one occurring prematurely. The two closely related meanings, "abnormal birth" and "untimely birth," express the same central idea.

word:greek-nt:G1723.explanation: Enankalizomai means to take someone in your arms or embrace them.

word:greek-nt:G1781.explanation: Entellō means to give orders or commands.

word:greek-nt:G1864.explanation: This word means to contend: to make an active effort in support of something rather than remain passive. It describes purposeful engagement in a matter, with the sense of standing firmly for what is being upheld. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Jude 1:3. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic meaning is clear: to contend actively and earnestly.

word:greek-nt:G1886.explanation: Epaulis means a dwelling, habitation, or residence—a place to live.

word:greek-nt:G1961.explanation: Epimeno means to remain or stay. It can also mean to persist in something.

word:greek-nt:G2090.explanation: Hetoimazō means to make ready or prepare. The disciples prepared to eat the Passover.

word:greek-nt:G2173.explanation: Euchrēstos means useful, serviceable, or profitable.

word:greek-nt:G2216.explanation: Zorobabel is a personal name, also rendered Zerubbabel. The person bearing this name is identified as Shealtiel’s son and Abiud’s father.

word:greek-nt:G2339.explanation: Thēra means a trap or means of capture.

word:greek-nt:G2362.explanation: Thronos means a throne or seat.

word:greek-nt:G2432.explanation: Hilarotes means cheerfulness. It describes showing mercy cheerfully.

word:greek-nt:G2469.explanation: Iscariot is the surname of Judas.

word:greek-nt:G2487.explanation: Ichnos means a track, footstep, or step.

word:greek-nt:G2520.explanation: This Greek New Testament word means “be fit,” “being fit,” or “to be fitting.” It describes something that is appropriate, suitable, or properly matching the situation. The word functions as an expression of what is fitting rather than naming a person, object, or event. It occurs twice in the Greek New Testament, so it is relatively uncommon there. Its exact force in either passage depends on the surrounding sentence and context.

word:greek-nt:G2555.explanation: Kakopoios means an evildoer, someone who does evil.

word:greek-nt:G2634.explanation: Katakyrieuō means to exercise authority over or master others. It can also mean to overpower people.

word:greek-nt:G2836.explanation: Koilia means the belly or abdomen. It can also refer to the stomach or the womb.

word:greek-nt:G2995.explanation: Larynx means the throat or gullet.

word:greek-nt:G3000.explanation: Latreuo means to serve, especially God.

word:greek-nt:G3075.explanation: Lymainō means to ravage or destroy, describing harsh mistreatment that damages or corrupts what is attacked.

word:greek-nt:G3109.explanation: Makedonia means Macedonia, a Roman province north of Achaia.

word:greek-nt:G3152.explanation: Mataios means vain, futile, ineffective, or worthless—describing something that produces no useful result.

word:greek-nt:G3318.explanation: Mesopotamia is the name of a region. The word functions as a place-name rather than describing an action, quality, or person. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs twice, both times in Acts. It is rendered “Mesopotamia” and refers to the geographic region associated with the biblical account. The word appears in Acts 2:9 and Acts 7:2, but understanding its particular significance in either passage requires the surrounding verse and passage context.

word:greek-nt:G3321.explanation: Mesouranēma means mid-heaven, the middle of heaven.

word:greek-nt:G3383.explanation: Mēte means neither or nor, joining alternatives in a negative statement.

word:greek-nt:G3592.explanation: Hode means “this” or “that.” It can point to something specific, as in “these things.”

word:greek-nt:G3633.explanation: Oiomai means to think or suppose.

word:greek-nt:G3691.explanation: Oxys means sharp. It can also describe something as swift.

word:greek-nt:G3725.explanation: Horion means the boundaries of a place, or a district or region.

word:greek-nt:G3750.explanation: This word means the sense of smell—the ability by which a person or creature detects odors. It refers to one of the bodily senses, alongside seeing, hearing, tasting, and touching. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in 1 Corinthians 12:17. The word itself identifies the faculty of smelling; its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding context, which is not included here.

word:greek-nt:G3974.explanation: Paphos is a city at the western end of Cyprus.

word:greek-nt:G4092.explanation: Pimprēmi means to swell or swell up.

word:greek-nt:G4250.explanation: Prin means before, indicating that one event or action occurs earlier than another.

word:greek-nt:G4333.explanation: Prosergazomai means to gain more or produce in addition.

word:greek-nt:G4391.explanation: Prouparchō means to have been already or to have existed previously.

word:greek-nt:G4409.explanation: Prōteuō means to have preeminence—to be first or supreme.

word:greek-nt:G4500.explanation: Rhoizedon means with a great noise, a rushing sound, or a roar.

word:greek-nt:G4575.explanation: Sebastos means revered or august. It can also serve as a title for Augustus, the emperor.

word:greek-nt:G4683.explanation: Sparganoō means to wrap or swathe in swaddling clothes.

word:greek-nt:G4746.explanation: Stoikos means a bough or branch of a tree.

word:greek-nt:G4863.explanation: Synagō means to gather together, collect, or assemble. It can describe people being brought together, as when a multitude gathered in one place.

word:greek-nt:G5002.explanation: This word means “appointed,” referring to something fixed, designated, or set in place. It describes an arrangement established for a particular purpose or time rather than something accidental or spontaneous. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Acts 12:21, and its precise force there depends on the surrounding verse and passage. The word therefore emphasizes being assigned or established according to a prior designation. It does not by itself explain who made the appointment or why; those details must come from the context.

word:greek-nt:G5059.explanation: Teras means a wonder or marvel. It describes wonders shown alongside signs, and many wonders were done through the apostles.

word:greek-nt:G5288.explanation: Hypostellō means to withdraw or draw back, to hold back, or to shun.

word:greek-nt:G5330.explanation: Pharisaios means Pharisee, a member of a Jewish sect.

word:greek-nt:G5345.explanation: Pheme means a report or fame. It can also refer to news that spreads.

word:greek-nt:G5543.explanation: Chrestos means kind. It can also describe something easy. It can also describe what is good.
